116|```json
117|{
118|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
119|  "version": "1.0.0",
120|  "parameters": {
121|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
122|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
123|  },
124|  "components": [
125|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
126|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
127|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
128|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
129|  ],
130|  "tripwires": [
131|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
132|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
133|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
134|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
135|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
136|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
137|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
138|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
139|  ],
140|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
141|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
142|}
143|```
144|
145|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
146|
147|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
148|
149|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
150|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
151|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
152|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
153|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
154|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
155|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
156|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
157|
158|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
159|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
160|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
161|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
162|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
163|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
164|
165|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
166|
167|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
168|
169|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
170|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
171|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
172|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
173|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
174|
175|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
176|
177|### 6.1 The loop
178|
179|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
180|
181|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
182|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
183|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
184|- **Ending.**
185|
186|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
187|| --- | --- | --- |
188|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
189|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
190|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
191|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
192|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
193|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
194|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
195|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
196|
197|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
198|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
199|
200|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
201|
202|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
203|
204|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
205|| --- | --- | --- |
206|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
207|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
208|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
209|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
210|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
211|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
212|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
213|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
214|
215|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
216|
217|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
218|
219|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
220|| --- | --- | --- |
221|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
222|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
223|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
224|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |

252|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
253|  "action": {
254|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
255|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
256|    "resource": "full resource name",
257|    "updateMask": ["field"],
258|    "patch": {},

260|  },

262|  "rollback": "string",

269|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
270|
271|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
272|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
273|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.

277|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.

279|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.

282|| --- | --- |
283|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
284|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
285|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
286|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
287|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |

291|### 6.6 Guardrails
292|
293|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
294|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
295|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
296|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
297|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
298|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
299|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
300|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.

435|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. At each tick instant, as built: `scheduler.tick()`, `world.step_until(t)`, ingest every new sink entry in write order, `evaluator.tick()`. A canary planted at a tick can be fetched by a run at the same instant.
436|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.
437|3. **Matching and latency.** Actual events match expected ones on (deployment, tripwire). Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
438|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.
439|5. **Routing.** Entries route to a deployment by the component's `container_name` and `match` labels, then `deploymentBy`; a connector label maps through `Deployment.resources`, with `jsonPayload.environment` as the fallback.
440|6. **Arming.** `${param}` is resolved when a deployment is armed. Cadence and canary are evaluated in `tick()`, schema and errorSignature in `ingest()`. Every `TripEvent.at` is `clock.now()`. The evaluator keeps only the runs a window needs.
441|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
442|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.
443|9. **Canary scheduler** plants through `World.plant_canary`, first at arm + `everyMinutes`, then every `everyMinutes`, only for deployments whose contract has a synthetic tripwire.
444|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).
445|11. **Cost.** The scenario-library tests share module-scoped scorecards.
446|12. **Known weakness.** With errorSignature recovery after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs, `flap-severe` (rate 0.7) passes on its seed partly by luck: about 2 seeds in 3 would see a 3-clean streak and a recovery. A symmetric rule (recover when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are clean) is more robust; deferred until after the hackathon.

50|### 3.2 Connector runtime (emulates the SOAR `python` container)
51|
52|One worker per connector instance. Every `intervalSeconds` (while `enabled` and not stalled):
53|
54|1. Get a token from the fake token endpoint using the instance's `Client Secret` parameter.
55|2. Fetch incidents since the stored checkpoint (dedupe by `providerIncidentId`).
56|3. Map each incident to an `AlertInfo` (faithful field names, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/respond/ide/creating-a-custom-connector)):
57|   - `name` ← `properties.title`
58|   - `ticket_id` / `display_id` ← `properties.providerIncidentId`
59|   - `rule_generator` ← first label or `"Sentinel Analytics"` (must not be empty)
60|   - `priority` ← severity map: `High→80`, `Medium→60`, `Low→40`, `Informational→-1` (Google's scale is Informative −1, Low 40, Medium 60, High 80, Critical 100)

So `dead-connector` measures whether the connector ran, and `connector-errors` whether it ran cleanly.

95|### 3.4 Job runtime (intel-sync)
96|
97|One worker per job instance. Every `intervalSeconds`: fetch indicators from a fake TI feed (`/_upstream/{env}/indicators?lookbackHours=N`), "sync" them, write a `python` log entry `job.run.completed` with `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` and `jsonPayload.status`, and append a `JobInstanceLog` (`status` `SUCCESS`/`ERROR`, `message`, `startTime`, `endTime`). 109|
110|`POST /_upstream/{env}/incidents:plant` creates an incident whose title starts with `[CANARY]` and whose `providerIncidentId` is `canary-<uuid>`. 433|**Semantics settled in D4.** Pinned by the D4 tests or decided in the implementation and accepted in review.
434|
435|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. At each tick instant, as built: `scheduler.tick()`, `world.step_until(t)`, ingest every new sink entry in write order, `evaluator.tick()`. A canary planted at a tick can be fetched by a run at the same instant.
436|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.
437|3. **Matching and latency.** Actual events match expected ones on (deployment, tripwire). Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
438|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.
439|5. **Routing.** Entries route to a deployment by the component's `container_name` and `match` labels, then `deploymentBy`; a connector label maps through `Deployment.resources`, with `jsonPayload.environment` as the fallback.
440|6. **Arming.** `${param}` is resolved when a deployment is armed. Cadence and canary are evaluated in `tick()`, schema and errorSignature in `ingest()`. Every `TripEvent.at` is `clock.now()`. The evaluator keeps only the runs a window needs.
441|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
442|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.
443|9. **Canary scheduler** plants through `World.plant_canary`, first at arm + `everyMinutes`, then every `everyMinutes`, only for deployments whose contract has a synthetic tripwire.
444|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).
445|11. **Cost.** The scenario-library tests share module-scoped scorecards.
446|12. **Known weakness.** With errorSignature recovery after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs, `flap-severe` (rate 0.7) passes on its seed partly by luck: about 2 seeds in 3 would see a 3-clean streak and a recovery. A symmetric rule (recover when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are clean) is more robust; deferred until after the hackathon.

21|## 1. Summary
22|
23|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires, proposes a fix for a human to approve, and amends the contract when an incident exposes a gap. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
24|
25|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
26|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools, proposes allowlisted actions, writes the postmortem and drafts contract amendments.
27|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
28|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service.
29|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, deployed to a personal GCP project (Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, IAM, Cloud Run, Firestore).
30|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
31|
32|## 2. Design principles
33|
34|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
35|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
36|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
37|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
38|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
39|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
40|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
41|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
42|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
43|
44|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.

46|## 3. The SRE loop
47|
48|The model acts at three points (author, investigate, close). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
49|
50|```mermaid
51|flowchart LR
52|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
53|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
54|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
55|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
56|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
57|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
58|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
59|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
60|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
61|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
62|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
63|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (SRE postmortem)"]
64|  J -- "gap found: amend" --> A
65|```
66|
67|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
68|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
69|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
70|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
71|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
72|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
73|7. **Close and learn.** The SRE writes a postmortem. If the incident exposed a gap (a late or missing trip), it drafts an amendment, which goes back through the scorecard and approval and then applies to every deployment of that service.

112|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
113|
114|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
115|
116|```json
117|{
118|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
119|  "version": "1.0.0",
120|  "parameters": {
121|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
122|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
123|  },
124|  "components": [
125|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
126|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
127|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
128|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
129|  ],
130|  "tripwires": [
131|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
132|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
133|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
134|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
135|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
136|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
137|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
138|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
139|  ],
140|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
141|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
142|}
143|```
144|
145|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
146|
147|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
148|
149|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
150|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
151|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
152|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
153|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
154|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
155|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
156|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
157|
158|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
159|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
160|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
161|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
162|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
163|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
164|
165|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.

167|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
168|
169|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
170|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
171|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
172|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
173|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.

175|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
176|
177|### 6.1 The loop
178|
179|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
180|
181|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
182|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
183|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
184|- **Ending.**
185|
186|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
187|| --- | --- | --- |
188|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
189|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
190|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
191|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
192|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
193|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
194|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
195|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
196|
197|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
198|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
199|
200|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
201|
202|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
203|
204|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
205|| --- | --- | --- |
206|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
207|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
208|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
209|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
210|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
211|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
212|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
213|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |

215|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
216|
217|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
218|
219|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
220|| --- | --- | --- |
221|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
222|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
223|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
224|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |

241|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
242|
243|```json
244|{
245|  "incidentId": "string",
246|  "deployment": "string",
247|  "component": "string",
248|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
249|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
250|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
251|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
252|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
253|  "action": {
254|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
255|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
256|    "resource": "full resource name",
257|    "updateMask": ["field"],
258|    "patch": {},
259|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
260|  },
261|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
262|  "rollback": "string",
263|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
264|}

266|
267|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
268|
269|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
270|
271|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
272|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
273|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
274|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
275|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
276|
277|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
278|
279|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
280|
281|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
282|| --- | --- |
283|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
284|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
285|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
286|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
287|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
288|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
289|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |

291|### 6.6 Guardrails
292|
293|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
294|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
295|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
296|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
297|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
298|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
299|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
300|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.

78|## Gates
79|
80|25. **Problem strings** take the form `<rule>: <text>`. Rules:
81|    - Order and hypotheses: `order`, `hypotheses.count`, `hypotheses.alternative`, `hypotheses.id`.
82|    - Evidence: `evidence.insert_id`, `evidence.deployment`, `evidence.future`, `evidence.call_id`, `evidence.field`, `evidence.value`, `evidence.hypothesis`, `evidence.limit`.
83|    - Diagnosis:
84|      - `diagnosis.schema`, with the JSON path of the problem (`diagnosis.schema: action: 'type' is a required property`). Argument-validation errors inside `diagnosis` use this rule, not `args.schema`.
85|      - `diagnosis.evidence`
86|      - `diagnosis.coverage`
87|      - `diagnosis.category` (includes `unknown` without `escalate`)
88|      - `diagnosis.action` (method outside the allowlist; empty `escalationSummary`)
89|      - `diagnosis.update_mask` (mask outside the method's fields, or patch keys outside the mask)
90|      - `diagnosis.resource`
91|      - `diagnosis.incident` (`incidentId` or `deployment`)
92|      - `diagnosis.component`, listing the contract's component IDs
93|      - `diagnosis.hypothesis`
94|      - `diagnosis.verification` (missing, or a tripwire not of this deployment)
95|      - `diagnosis.none_after_resume`
96|    - Other: `reads.cap`, `tool.unknown`, `tool.name`, `tool.error`, `args.schema` (with the JSON path).
97|26. **`set_hypotheses`.** Items are `{id, statement, wouldConfirm, alternative}`, all four required. IDs match `^H[1-9][0-9]*$` and are unique. 2–4 items, at least one alternative. Replacing the set keeps evidence whose hypothesis ID remains.
98|27. **`record_evidence`.**
99|    - **Log source:** the insertId exists, its timestamp is ≤ now, and it routes (via `Registry.route`) to the incident's deployment or to a sibling queried in this session (via `query_logs` on it, or `compare_siblings`). There is no other fallback.
100|    - **Tool source:** `callId` is an accepted read-tool call of this session. `field` is a dotted path into the result, where numeric segments index lists and a leading `result.` is stripped. `value` must match by JSON equality, with no coercion.
101|    - At most 3 items per hypothesis. IDs are `E<n>`, and `recordedAtTurn` is the session turn.
102|28. **`submit_diagnosis`** checks, in addition to spec §6.5:
103|    - The schema first. A schema problem always refuses, gates on or off. With gates on and no hypotheses yet, the order problem is reported first.
104|    - `incidentId` and `deployment` equal the incident's.
105|    - `component` is a component ID of the deployment's contract.
106|    - `hypothesis` is a current hypothesis.
107|    - For `propose`: a `connectorInstances.*` method needs the deployment's connector instance name, and a `jobInstances.*` method its job instance name, by exact match. The integration instance is never a valid resource. The patch keys are within `updateMask`.
108|    - `expectedVerification` is required for `propose` and `none`, and optional for `escalate`.
109|    - For `none`: an item counts as recorded after the last resume iff `recordedAtTurn > max(resumed_at_turns)`. With no resume, every item counts.
110|    - Repeated submissions to the ToolSet are allowed; the loop ends at the first accepted one.
111|29. **Category rules** (the spec §6.5 table, tightened):
112|    - `connector_stalled` / `job_stalled`: the cited log evidence includes, by insertId, the deployment's latest heartbeat at or before `trip_event.at`. The heartbeat is the event of the cadence tripwire on the contract's `connectorInstance` (`jobInstance`) component, whatever the incident's component, so a canary incident can be diagnosed `connector_stalled`.
113|    - `credential_failure`: an entry from the deployment's connector at or above WARNING, plus a `test_integration_instance` call on the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false`.
114|    - `schema_drift`: an entry that routes to the incident's deployment and for which `evaluator.tripwires.schema_violation` returns a reason. `schema_violation` applies the tripwire's `event`/`where` filters itself; `${param}` is resolved.
115|    - `job_hollow_success`: a `job.run.completed` of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0`.
116|    - `job_failing`: a `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` with `status: ERROR`, of the deployment.
117|30. **`verification=False`.** The order, hypotheses, evidence and diagnosis rules 2–5 record `wouldRefuse`, with their problems, instead of refusing. Schema problems (`args.schema`, `diagnosis.schema`) still refuse. Budgets, the read cap and stuck still apply.
118|31. **The right component** for evaluation is the tripped tripwire's component.

50|### 3.2 Connector runtime (emulates the SOAR `python` container)
51|
52|One worker per connector instance. Every `intervalSeconds` (while `enabled` and not stalled):
53|
54|1. Get a token from the fake token endpoint using the instance's `Client Secret` parameter.
55|2. Fetch incidents since the stored checkpoint (dedupe by `providerIncidentId`).
56|3. Map each incident to an `AlertInfo` (faithful field names, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/respond/ide/creating-a-custom-connector)):
57|   - `name` ← `properties.title`
58|   - `ticket_id` / `display_id` ← `properties.providerIncidentId`
59|   - `rule_generator` ← first label or `"Sentinel Analytics"` (must not be empty)
60|   - `priority` ← severity map: `High→80`, `Medium→60`, `Low→40`, `Informational→-1` (Google's scale is Informative −1, Low 40, Medium 60, High 80, Critical 100)
61|   - unknown severity → the `Unknown Severity Priority` parameter if set, **otherwise the raw string is passed through** (this is the severity-drift bug)
62|   - `device_vendor = "Microsoft"`, `device_product = "Azure Sentinel"`
63|   - `start_time` / `end_time` ← first/last activity (unix ms)
64|   - `environment` ← the instance's environment
65|   - `events` ← one event dict per incident with `device_product`
66|4. Hand alerts to ingestion.
67|5. Emit logs (see §5) and, while log collection is on (§4.1), append `ConnectorLog` records. Every run ends with `connector.run.completed`, including a run that failed; a failed run writes `connector.run.warning` or `connector.run.error` first (invented). So `dead-connector` measures whether the connector ran, and `connector-errors` whether it ran cleanly.
68|
69|**Swallowed failure (Green Liar).** On a 401 from upstream, the worker catches the exception, writes a `WARNING` log (and, while log collection is on, a `WARNING` ConnectorLog) ("Failed to authenticate to Sentinel workspace: 401 Unauthorized"), returns zero alerts and still emits `connector.run.completed`. Status stays `LIVE`.

90|
91|Receives `AlertInfo` objects. 95|### 3.4 Job runtime (intel-sync)
96|
97|One worker per job instance. Every `intervalSeconds`: fetch indicators from a fake TI feed (`/_upstream/{env}/indicators?lookbackHours=N`), "sync" them, write a `python` log entry `job.run.completed` with `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` and `jsonPayload.status`, and append a `JobInstanceLog` (`status` `SUCCESS`/`ERROR`, `message`, `startTime`, `endTime`). Updates the job instance's `lastRunTime`, `lastRunStatus`, `nextScheduledRunTime`. A failed run writes `job.run.error` and then still ends with `job.run.completed` (`status: ERROR`, `indicatorsSynced: 0`, severity ERROR), so `dead-job` measures whether the job ran and `hollow-run` checks only `SUCCESS` runs (invented).

102|| --- | --- | --- | --- |

108|### 3.5 Canary planter
109|
110|`POST /_upstream/{env}/incidents:plant` creates an incident whose title starts with `[CANARY]` and whose `providerIncidentId` is `canary-<uuid>`. Ingestion sets `jsonPayload.alert.canary = true` for it. A canary counts as seen when an `alert.ingested` entry has `alert.canary: true` and `alert.ticket_id` equal to the planted `providerIncidentId`. Canaries are planted with severity `Informational`, so F3 never affects them. The platform's synthetic tripwire calls this endpoint; in production it would target only the `canary` environment (spec §5).

242|## 6. Fault catalog
243|
244|Each fault has a defined cause, what the native API shows, what should trip, and the **right answer**: the action a correct SRE takes. The right answers make the evaluations gradeable.
245|
246|| ID | Fault | Mock behaviour | Native API shows | Should trip | Right answer |
247|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
248|| F1 | `connector_stall` | Worker for one instance stops running. No logs, no ConnectorLogs | `status: LIVE`, `enabled: true` | `dead-connector` (cadence) | `connectorInstances.restart`. The mock clears a stall on any `enabled` false→true transition |
249|| F2 | `credential_expiry` | Upstream token endpoint returns 401 for one env. Connector swallows it: WARNING logs every run (and WARNING ConnectorLogs while log collection is on), zero alerts, runs on schedule | `status: LIVE`; `executeTest` → `successful: false`; the Logs tab is empty unless log collection is on | `connector-errors` (errorSignature), `canary` (synthetic) | `escalate`, category `credential_failure`. Siblings healthy → tenant-specific. Fix (rotate secret) is outside the allowlist |
250|| F3 | `severity_drift` | A fraction `rate` (fault `params`, e.g. 0.5) of new upstream incidents arrive with an unmapped severity (`"Critical"`); with `Unknown Severity Priority` empty, their `priority` becomes a string | `status: LIVE`, volume normal | `priority-shape` (schema) | `connectorInstances.patch` `parameters`: set `Unknown Severity Priority` to `100` (or `80`) |

252|| F5 | `job_error` | Fake TI feed returns 500; job runs end `ERROR` | `lastRunStatus: ERROR` | intel-sync `job-errors` (errorSignature) | `escalate`, category `job_failing` (upstream outage) |

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""Check that every deliverable ID has a matching acceptance test."""
3|
4|import argparse
5|import re
6|import sys
7|from pathlib import Path
8|
9|ID_RE = re.compile(r"\bD(\d+)-T(\d+)\b")
10|DIR_RE = re.compile(r"^d(\d+)$", re.IGNORECASE)
11|TEST_RE = re.compile(r"def\s+test_d(\d+)_t(\d+)_", re.IGNORECASE)
12|
13|
14|def collect_doc_ids(doc: Path) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
15|    text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
16|    return {(int(n), int(m)) for n, m in ID_RE.findall(text)}
17|
18|
19|def existing_deliverables(tests_root: Path) -> set[int]:
20|    found: set[int] = set()
21|    if not tests_root.is_dir():
22|        return found
23|    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
24|        if child.is_dir():
25|            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
26|            if match:
27|                found.add(int(match.group(1)))
28|    return found
29|
30|
31|def collect_test_ids(tests_root: Path, deliverable: int) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
32|    found: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
33|    target = None
34|    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
35|        if child.is_dir() and DIR_RE.match(child.name):
36|            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
37|            if match and int(match.group(1)) == deliverable:
38|                target = child
39|                break
40|    if target is None:
41|        return found
42|    for pyfile in target.rglob("*.py"):
43|        try:
44|            text = pyfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
45|        except OSError:
46|            continue
47|        for n, m in TEST_RE.findall(text):
48|            found.add((int(n), int(m)))
49|    return found
50|
51|
52|def main() -> int:
53|    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Trace deliverable IDs to tests.")
54|    parser.add_argument("--doc", required=True, help="Path to deliverables doc")
55|    parser.add_argument("--tests", required=True, help="Root of acceptance tests")
56|    args = parser.parse_args()
57|    doc = Path(args.doc)
58|    tests_root = Path(args.tests)
59|    if not doc.is_file():
60|        print(f"doc not found: {doc}", file=sys.stderr)
61|        return 2
62|    if not tests_root.is_dir():
63|        print(f"tests root not found: {tests_root}", file=sys.stderr)
64|        return 2
65|    doc_ids = collect_doc_ids(doc)
66|    present = existing_deliverables(tests_root)
67|    missing: list[str] = []
68|    for n, m in sorted(doc_ids):
69|        if n not in present:
70|            continue
71|        if (n, m) not in collect_test_ids(tests_root, n):
72|            missing.append(f"D{n}-T{m}")
73|    if missing:
74|        print("Missing tests for IDs:")
75|        for item in missing:
76|            print(f"  {item}")
77|        return 1
78|    return 0
79|
80|
81|if __name__ == "__main__":
82|    sys.exit(main())

11|TEST_RE = re.compile(r"def\s+test_d(\d+)_t(\d+)_", re.IGNORECASE)
12|
13|
14|def collect_doc_ids(doc: Path) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
15|    text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
16|    return {(int(n), int(m)) for n, m in ID_RE.findall(text)}
17|
18|
19|def existing_deliverables(tests_root: Path) -> set[int]:
20|    found: set[int] = set()
21|    if not tests_root.is_dir():
22|        return found
23|    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
24|        if child.is_dir():
25|            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
26|            if match:
27|                found.add(int(match.group(1)))
28|    return found
29|
30|
31|def collect_test_ids(tests_root: Path, deliverable: int) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
32|    found: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
33|    target = None
34|    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
35|        if child.is_dir() and DIR_RE.match(child.name):
36|            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
37|            if match and int(match.group(1)) == deliverable:
38|                target = child
39|                break
40|    if target is None:
41|        return found
42|    for pyfile in target.rglob("*.py"):
43|        try:
44|            text = pyfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
45|        except OSError:
46|            continue
47|        for n, m in TEST_RE.findall(text):
48|            found.add((int(n), int(m)))
49|    return found
50|
51|
52|def main() -> int:
53|    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Trace deliverable IDs to tests.")
54|    parser.add_argument("--doc", required=True, help="Path to deliverables doc")
55|    parser.add_argument("--tests", required=True, help="Root of acceptance tests")
56|    args = parser.parse_args()
57|    doc = Path(args.doc)
58|    tests_root = Path(args.tests)
59|    if not doc.is_file():
60|        print(f"doc not found: {doc}", file=sys.stderr)
61|        return 2
62|    if not tests_root.is_dir():
63|        print(f"tests root not found: {tests_root}", file=sys.stderr)
64|        return 2
65|    doc_ids = collect_doc_ids(doc)
66|    present = existing_deliverables(tests_root)
67|    missing: list[str] = []
68|    for n, m in sorted(doc_ids):
69|        if n not in present:
70|            continue
71|        if (n, m) not in collect_test_ids(tests_root, n):
72|            missing.append(f"D{n}-T{m}")
73|    if missing:
74|        print("Missing tests for IDs:")
75|        for item in missing:
76|            print(f"  {item}")
77|        return 1
78|    return 0
79|
80|
81|if __name__ == "__main__":
82|    sys.exit(main())

343|def investigate(
344|    incident: Any,
345|    tools: Any,
346|    gateway: Any,
347|    store: Any,
348|    *,
349|    max_turns: int = 24,
350|    max_read_calls: int = 12,
351|    max_tokens: int = 400_000,
352|) -> InvestigationResult:
353|    """Run or continue an investigation (d5-pins.md pin 9)."""
354|    try:
355|        session = store.load(incident.id)
356|    except KeyError:
357|        session = None
358|    if session is None:
359|        session = Session(
360|            incident_id=incident.id,
361|            turn_limit=max_turns,
362|            read_limit=max_read_calls,
363|            token_limit=max_tokens,
364|            transcript_id=f"tx-{incident.id}",
365|            history=[
366|                {"role": "developer", "content": _read_prompt()},
367|                {
368|                    "role": "user",
369|                    "content": render_incident(
370|                        incident, tools.registry
371|                    ),
372|                },
373|            ],
374|        )
375|    elif session.status != "running":
376|        raise ValueError(
377|            f"investigation for {incident.id} already ended "
378|            f"({session.status}/{session.reason}); needs_input "
379|            "sessions resume only through resume()"
380|        )
381|    else:
382|        session.turn_limit = session.segment_start_turn + max_turns
383|        session.read_limit = max_read_calls
384|        session.token_limit = max_tokens
385|        store.save(session)
386|    return _run(incident, tools, gateway, store, session)

389|def resume(
390|    incident: Any,
391|    tools: Any,
392|    gateway: Any,
393|    store: Any,
394|    *,
395|    message: str,
396|    extra_turns: int = 8,
397|    extra_reads: int = 4,
398|) -> InvestigationResult:
399|    """Resume a paused investigation with a new segment (d5-pins.md pin 9)."""
400|    session = store.load(incident.id)
401|    if session.status != "needs_input":
402|        raise ValueError(
403|            f"cannot resume incident {incident.id} with status "
404|            f"{session.status}; only needs_input sessions resume"
405|        )
406|    session.segment_start_turn = session.turn
407|    session.turn_limit = session.turn + extra_turns
408|    session.read_limit = extra_reads
409|    session.segment_reads = 0
410|    session.segment_tokens = 0
411|    session.refused_submissions = 0
412|    session.resumed_at_turns.append(session.turn)
413|    session.status = "running"
414|    session.reason = ""
415|    session.history.append({"role": "user", "content": message})
416|    store.save(session)
417|    return _run(incident, tools, gateway, store, session)

343|def investigate(
344|    incident: Any,
345|    tools: Any,
346|    gateway: Any,
347|    store: Any,
348|    *,
349|    max_turns: int = 24,
350|    max_read_calls: int = 12,
351|    max_tokens: int = 400_000,
352|) -> InvestigationResult:
353|    """Run or continue an investigation (d5-pins.md pin 9)."""
354|    try:
355|        session = store.load(incident.id)
356|    except KeyError:
357|        session = None
358|    if session is None:
359|        session = Session(
360|            incident_id=incident.id,
361|            turn_limit=max_turns,
362|            read_limit=max_read_calls,
363|            token_limit=max_tokens,
364|            transcript_id=f"tx-{incident.id}",
365|            history=[
366|                {"role": "developer", "content": _read_prompt()},
367|                {
368|                    "role": "user",
369|                    "content": render_incident(
370|                        incident, tools.registry
371|                    ),
372|                },
373|            ],
374|        )
375|    elif session.status != "running":
376|        raise ValueError(
377|            f"investigation for {incident.id} already ended "
378|            f"({session.status}/{session.reason}); needs_input "
379|            "sessions resume only through resume()"
380|        )
381|    else:
382|        session.turn_limit = session.segment_start_turn + max_turns
383|        session.read_limit = max_read_calls
384|        session.token_limit = max_tokens
385|        store.save(session)
386|    return _run(incident, tools, gateway, store, session)

389|def resume(
390|    incident: Any,
391|    tools: Any,
392|    gateway: Any,
393|    store: Any,
394|    *,
395|    message: str,
396|    extra_turns: int = 8,
397|    extra_reads: int = 4,
398|) -> InvestigationResult:
399|    """Resume a paused investigation with a new segment (d5-pins.md pin 9)."""
400|    session = store.load(incident.id)
401|    if session.status != "needs_input":
402|        raise ValueError(
403|            f"cannot resume incident {incident.id} with status "
404|            f"{session.status}; only needs_input sessions resume"
405|        )
406|    session.segment_start_turn = session.turn
407|    session.turn_limit = session.turn + extra_turns
408|    session.read_limit = extra_reads
409|    session.segment_reads = 0
410|    session.segment_tokens = 0
411|    session.refused_submissions = 0
412|    session.resumed_at_turns.append(session.turn)
413|    session.status = "running"
414|    session.reason = ""
415|    session.history.append({"role": "user", "content": message})
416|    store.save(session)
417|    return _run(incident, tools, gateway, store, session)

716|        deployment: str,
717|        component: str,
718|        *,

731|        scoped = {

734|            if any(
735|                t.id == tw_id and t.component == component
736|                for t in contract.tripwires
737|            )
738|        }

18|    service: str

25|def deployments_from_fleet(
26|    fleet: "FleetConfig",
27|    contract: "Contract",
28|    environments: Sequence[str] | None = None,
29|) -> list[Deployment]:
30|    """Build armed deployments for a service from a loaded fleet.
31|
32|    Parameters come from the fleet's deployment entries. ``resources``
33|    maps component id to the fleet's resource instance id, matched by
34|    component kind (connectorInstance -> connectorInstance,
35|    jobInstance -> jobInstance); components without a fleet instance id
36|    (e.g. ETL flows) have no entry.
37|    """
38|    if environments is None:
39|        envs = sorted(
40|            env
41|            for env, spec in fleet.environments.items()
42|            if contract.service in spec.deployments
43|        )
44|    else:
45|        envs = list(environments)
46|    connectors: dict[str, str] = {}
47|    jobs: dict[str, str] = {}
48|    for integ_name, spec in fleet.integrations.items():
49|        if not isinstance(spec, dict):
50|            continue
51|        for key in spec.get("connectors", {}):
52|            connectors.setdefault(integ_name, key)
53|        for key in spec.get("jobs", {}):
54|            jobs.setdefault(integ_name, key)
55|    deployments: list[Deployment] = []
56|    for env in envs:
57|        dep = fleet.environments[env].deployments[contract.service]
58|        resources: dict[str, str] = {}
59|        resource_names: dict[str, str] = {}
60|        used_integration: str | None = None
61|        for component in contract.components:
62|            if (
63|                component.kind == "connectorInstance"
64|                and dep.connectorInstance
65|                and connectors
66|            ):
67|                resources[component.id] = dep.connectorInstance
68|                integ = next(iter(connectors))
69|                used_integration = integ
70|                resource_names[component.id] = (
71|                    f"{fleet.instance}/integrations/{integ}/connectors/"
72|                    f"{connectors[integ]}/connectorInstances/"
73|                    f"{dep.connectorInstance}"
74|                )
75|            elif component.kind == "jobInstance" and dep.jobInstance and jobs:
76|                resources[component.id] = dep.jobInstance
77|                integ = next(iter(jobs))
78|                used_integration = integ
79|                resource_names[component.id] = (
80|                    f"{fleet.instance}/integrations/{integ}/jobs/"
81|                    f"{jobs[integ]}/jobInstances/{dep.jobInstance}"
82|                )
83|        if used_integration is not None:
84|            resource_names["integrationInstance"] = (
85|                f"{fleet.instance}/integrations/{used_integration}/"
86|                f"integrationInstances/{env}"
87|            )
88|        deployments.append(
89|            Deployment(
90|                id=f"{contract.service}/{env}",
91|                service=contract.service,
92|                environment=env,
93|                parameters=dict(dep.parameters),
94|                resources=resources,
95|                resource_names=resource_names,
96|            )
97|        )
98|    return deployments

101|# Fixed Chronicle resource prefix (docs/mocks.md §4.1). Full resource names
102|# come from the fleet via Deployment.resource_names, never from copies here.
103|CHRONICLE_PREFIX = "projects/fleet-sre-demo/locations/us/instances/mock-soar"

106|class Registry:
107|    """Contracts + deployments + scorecards with log routing (spec.md §4.1)."""
108|
109|    def __init__(
110|        self,
111|        contracts: list["Contract"],
112|        deployments: list[Deployment],
113|        scorecards: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
114|    ) -> None:
115|        self._contracts = {c.service: c for c in contracts}
116|        self._deployments = {d.id: d for d in deployments}
117|        self._by_service: dict[str, list[Deployment]] = {}
118|        for dep in deployments:
119|            self._by_service.setdefault(dep.service, []).append(dep)
120|        self._scorecards = dict(scorecards) if scorecards else {}
121|
122|    @property
123|    def services(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
124|        return tuple(self._contracts)
125|
126|    def contract(self, service: str) -> "Contract":
127|        return self._contracts[service]
128|
129|    def deployments(self, service: str) -> list[Deployment]:
130|        return list(self._by_service.get(service, []))
131|
132|    def deployment(self, id: str) -> Deployment:
133|        return self._deployments[id]
134|
135|    def scorecard(self, service: str) -> Any:
136|        return self._scorecards.get(service)
137|
138|    def route(self, entry: LogEntry) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
139|        """Route an entry to [(deployment ID, component ID)].
140|
141|        Uses the evaluator's routing (deliverables.md §D4 item 5):
142|        the component's container_name and match labels, then
143|        deploymentBy; a connector label maps through
144|        Deployment.resources, with jsonPayload.environment as fallback.
145|        """
146|        found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
147|        container = entry.resource.labels.get("container_name")
148|        for service, contract in self._contracts.items():
149|            for component in contract.components:
150|                if component.logs.container_name != container:
151|                    continue
152|                if any(
153|                    key not in entry.labels
154|                    for key in component.logs.match
155|                ):
156|                    continue
157|                dep_id = self._resolve(
158|                    service, component.id, component.logs.deploymentBy,
159|                    entry,
160|                )
161|                if dep_id is not None:
162|                    found.append((dep_id, component.id))
163|        return found
164|
165|    def _resolve(
166|        self, service: str, component_id: str, deployment_by: str,
167|        entry: LogEntry,
168|    ) -> str | None:
169|        if deployment_by.startswith("labels."):
170|            value = entry.labels.get(deployment_by[len("labels."):])
171|            if value is not None:
172|                for dep in self._by_service.get(service, []):
173|                    if dep.resources.get(component_id) == value:
174|                        return dep.id
175|            return self._env_fallback(service, entry)
176|        if deployment_by.startswith("jsonPayload."):
177|            node: Any = entry.jsonPayload
178|            for part in deployment_by.split(".")[1:]:
179|                if isinstance(node, dict) and part in node:
180|                    node = node[part]
181|                else:
182|                    return None
183|            if not isinstance(node, str):
184|                return None
185|            dep_id = f"{service}/{node}"
186|            return dep_id if dep_id in self._deployments else None
187|        return None
188|
189|    def _env_fallback(self, service: str, entry: LogEntry) -> str | None:
190|        env = entry.jsonPayload.get("environment")
191|        if not isinstance(env, str):
192|            return None
193|        dep_id = f"{service}/{env}"
194|        return dep_id if dep_id in self._deployments else None

19|        return self._identity
20|
